newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes ailing in the face of oversupply.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes ailing in the face of oversupply.

text.p: Sickly North Sea crude values deteriorated further on Wednesday in the face of persistent prompt oversupply, traders said.
"There is genuine oversupply at the moment. Margins are good but there's only so much crude you can run and the contango isn't deep enough to start filling storage," said a trader.
Dated Brent traded at a weak May Brent less 80 cents and other grades saw discount to the benchmark grade widen.
Gas oil-rich Oseberg traded twice, at Dated less 30 and 34 cents a barrel, but even grades with higher gasoline yields, seasonally better placed, lost more ground, traders said.
Ekofisk loading in the middle of April fetched Dated less three cents, six cents cheaper than a cargo loading April 19-21 which traded on Tuesday.
Forties also slipped back, fetching Dated less 10 cents a barrel with early pricing, equivalent to nearer Dated less 15 cents.
Traders said the prospect of Brent moving to the United States was providing sellers with a glimmer of hope but others said that alone would not be enough to lift differentials.
Brent paper markets reflected the weaker tone, next week's CFDs slipping three cents to trade at May Brent -58 cents.

In the Mediterranean, sellers and buyers alike saw little sign of a turnaround in the crude supply/demand balance in the short term and some sellers were already offering below last done on almost all grades.
One Urals seller was offering at Dated Brent -$1.40 a barrel cif Augusta, and most expected the next deal at -$1.45, almost 10 cents weaker than trade on Monday.
Traders said Iraqi Kirkuk was quietly offered at the Official Selling Price (OSP) of Dated -$1.90 fob Ceyhan.
A second decade April Syrian Light cargo was heard to have traded at OSP evens, or Dated Brent -95 cents on Tuesday.
